title: `sendReport()` and `sendFeatureReport()` should clarify `data` payload contents and validate maximum report length
body:
### What is the issue with the WebHID Standard?

Currently, the steps for [`sendReport(reportId, data)`](https://hid.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-hiddevice-sendreport) and [`sendFeatureReport(reportId, data)`](https://hid.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-hiddevice-sendfeaturereport) check whether `reportId` is `0` vs. non-`0` in step 3 (rejecting with `TypeError`), and then pass `reportId` and `data` directly to the operating system in step 5.2. Neither method states explicitly that `data` excludes the 1-byte `reportId` prefix when the interface [uses report IDs](https://hid.spec.whatwg.org/#uses-report-ids) (unlike [`HIDInputReportEvent.data`](https://hid.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-hidinputreportevent-data)), and neither specifies how buffers larger than the declared report size should be handled. In addition, [`receiveFeatureReport(reportId)`](https://hid.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-hiddevice-receivefeaturereport) returns a `DataView` that *includes* the `reportId` byte at index `0`, which has led developers to pass an `N + 1`-byte buffer (including the report ID length) back into `sendFeatureReport(reportId, data)` (e.g. https://crbug.com/40164991#comment12, https://crbug.com/578562500).

When an oversized `data` buffer is passed to the operating system, platform behavior diverges: Windows accepts buffers larger than `HIDP_CAPS`'s report byte length and ignores trailing bytes, whereas macOS rejects writes exceeding the declared report size and Linux forwards the caller's full length. Chromium has historically rejected `sendReport()` calls when `data` exceeds the device's maximum output report payload size, and in Chrome 156 (https://crrev.com/c/8400910) added the matching check to `sendFeatureReport()`, which surfaced https://crbug.com/578562500 on Windows.

We should clarify in `sendReport()` and `sendFeatureReport()` that `data` contains only the report payload bytes (excluding the 1-byte `reportId` prefix, in contrast to `receiveFeatureReport()`). Beyond that, we should align on how the spec should handle `data` buffers larger than the report descriptor's declared size (related to #86 for undersized `sendReport()` buffers, and #108 for explicit report length overrides):

- **Validate upper bound in the browser**: Reject when `data` exceeds the interface/collection's maximum output or feature report payload size (`OutputReportByteLength` / `FeatureReportByteLength` on Windows `HIDP_CAPS`, per #86). This gives consistent cross-platform behavior instead of ignoring trailing bytes on Windows while failing on macOS (and if chosen, we should decide what error to fail with e.g. `NotAllowedError`). However, a hard browser-side cap blocks communicating with devices that ship with buggy, under-declared report descriptors (see https://crbug.com/40279476 and https://crbug.com/40164991#comment12) even on OS backends that would otherwise allow the transfer.
- **Pass through to the operating system without a browser cap**: Keep step 5.2 pass-through (and relax Chromium's browser-side max-size check in `sendReport()` / `sendFeatureReport()`) so devices with under-declared report descriptors remain usable where the underlying OS HID API permits oversized transfers, accepting that OS-level enforcement will continue to differ across Windows, macOS, and Linux (potentially paired with a console warning or an explicit length option as discussed in #108).
